blocking: Phone: the fixed Pause button sits over the Email input's bottom-left corner (index-phone-3) and over the footer's Instagram link (index-phone-4) at rest, breaking the owner's rule that controls never cover inputs or the footer; a parent tapping the field edge pauses motion instead.

fixes.what: On phones, keep the Pause button out of the content: either dock it in the header bar beside the menu toggle, or hide it (is-hidden) whenever .form or .site-footer intersects, not only while scrolling.
fixes.why: At rest it covers the email field and the footer links on 390px; the 64px reserves only protect the last line.

fixes.what: Change the link to 'Haldi & pheras, Anand Karaj, walima: every tradition, in its own words' so Hindu and Sikh families see themselves named on the home page.
fixes.why: The three slots are Persian, Muslim and Mehndi; a Hindu or Sikh parent gets no signal until the inner page.

fixes.where: index.html .promises (honoured, realised) vs about.html / weddings.html (honor, Honoring)
fixes.what: Pick one spelling site-wide; US spelling for a Bay Area studio: 'The elders honored, your vision realized.'
fixes.why: Mixed British and American spelling reads as two writers and chips at the premium polish.

fixes.what: Keep 'Elders' seats held at the front' once in the page intro and cut it from the six sections; trim 'as your family keeps it' from ~15 uses to one per section at most.
fixes.why: The repetition reads as a template, and parents skimming lose the ritual-specific lines underneath.

fixes.what: Start the statement eyebrow and h2 at the canopy's underside (row ~1200) instead of below it, so the second screen is never a full viewport of foliage with no words (index-desktop-1).
fixes.why: On desktop a parent sees one whole screen of painting and may think the page has stalled before any promise appears.

fixes.what: Footer address: put 'Anar Events · San Francisco Bay Area' on its own line with nowrap or shorten to 'San Francisco Bay Area' so 'Area' does not wrap alone (index-desktop-4).
fixes.why: A dangling single word in the address is the first thing a parent reads before dialing.
